result.title: Class-Conditional Conformal Triage for ICAO Face-Image Compliance under Class Imbalance
result.summary: Automated ICAO/ISO face-image compliance analysers provide criterion-level pass/fail decisions, yet these verdicts do not quantify uncertainty when deciding whether to accept, reject, or retake a photograph. We investigate conformal prediction as a triage layer for BioGaze, evaluating 14 compliance criteria on the synthetic TONO benchmark. Without retraining the analyser, we fit per-criterion logistic classifiers and compare marginal and label-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction with conventional abstention rules using subject-disjoint splits. Marginal conformal prediction achieved approximately 0.90 overall coverage but substantially under-covered violations, with a ten-partition mean of 0.37 for one criterion. The corresponding Mondrian means ranged from 0.89 to 0.92 across criteria. However, most of the reduction in criterion-level false positives came from the logistic layer (0.145 to 0.048), while tuned abstention rules achieved lower false-positive rates than Mondrian at comparable retake rates. Bonferroni correction for joint coverage across 14 criteria required retaking nearly all images. These findings show that class-conditional conformal prediction can achieve near-target empirical coverage for minority violation classes and reveal trade-offs between statistical coverage, classification performance, and retake requirements in multi-criterion face-image compliance assessment.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在合成 TONO 人脸图像基准上，把 conformal prediction 作为 BioGaze 合规分析器的「接受/拒绝/重拍」筛选层：不重训分析器，仅为 14 项合规标准各拟合 logistic 分类器，比较边际与 label-conditional（Mondrian）覆盖，并对照常规 abstention 规则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按类别校准的 conformal 覆盖与 abstention 规则可供核查能否迁移为 LVR 中按假设或视觉证据类别的停止、重查决策校准；结论提示覆盖率保证与分类性能、额外采样成本之间存在权衡，但与人脸合规任务本身无直接机制联系。
